defect_loop.failure: The prior report claimed manifestHash=packageArtifactHash while no package artifact, public schema, validator, or compiler existed in the tracked repository; live Consumer still displayed WAITING FOR PUBLIC CM2 CONTRACT.
defect_loop.fix: Tracked the public schema/compiler/package tools, emitted a canonical byte-verifiable artifact, added clean install tests, and projected only data decisions into an independent Consumer.
defect_loop.regression: Two clean builds/installs match; emitted and installed artifact hashes are identical; package tree contains no Lua.

defect_loop.failure: The first live Consumer start displayed PACKAGE MANIFEST V1 CONSUMER FAIL because Teardown's special root main.lua did not receive XML script params.
defect_loop.fix: Moved the host to MOD/script/testing/package_manifest/consumer_host.lua and attached parameters to a normal XML script node.
defect_loop.regression: A full Mod Manager/session restart loaded consumer-basic-v3 and displayed PASS with the installed package values.

defect_loop.failure: The validator preserved version ranges but did not evaluate resolved Core, SDK, or dependency versions.
defect_loop.fix: Added bounded semantic-version range evaluation and explicit compatibility/core-only report data.
defect_loop.regression: Compatible versions pass; incompatible Core, SDK and dependency cases each fail closed while preserving last-valid bytes.

scope_boundary: Step 9.1 proves the public data-only package contract and independent Teardown Consumer start. It does not claim that CM2 loads or instantiates the generated ship/weapon; the clean-room gameplay Runtime chain remains Step 9.3.
